# A Gantt example shows a project of 2,000 linked tasks

## Context

A leaf of #21346, the planning examples under #21140, and one of the three that the cut of Mon 23 Nov 2026 gets. The visitor's question: does the Gantt chart stay usable when the project has thousands of tasks?

No contributor labels: a maintainer builds it for the cut, and its first step is a profile whose result can change the scope.

## The Problem

`examples/gantt/basic` shows one phase with four tasks and two links. A real plan has hundreds to thousands of tasks, and scale is what a buyer checks first. The Gantt chart draws its task tree through the grid's buffered body; no example shows it under load.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/gantt/Container.mjs`: `taskColumns_` (`:70`), `cascadeDependencies_` (`:36`), `dependencyCreation` (`:38`), `useWorkingTime_` (`:72`). The stores: `src/gantt/TaskStore.mjs` (a tree store) and `src/gantt/DependencyStore.mjs`.
- **Two facts from [the source check on #21346](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21346#issuecomment-6982869553):** the link layer indexes every task and is not windowed vertically (`src/gantt/DependencyLayer.mjs:412-486`); and a parent task shows its stored dates, nothing derives them from its children (`src/gantt/Container.mjs:16-17`). Nothing has profiled the chart at this size.
- `examples/gantt/basic/Viewport.mjs` (135 lines) is the template: a toolbar, the chart, its two stores. It is not edited.
- The catalog: `apps/portal/resources/data/examples.json` (the record `gantt-basic` is the model); `publishes()` in `apps/portal/model/Example.mjs:133` drops a record without `image`.
- Specs for the family: `test/playwright/e2e/gantt/`.
- Design authority: n/a, a new example. Look, caption and cover follow the target in #21140's body.

## The Fix

1. **Profile first.** Put the data of step 2 into a scratch copy of the base example and measure first paint, expanding and collapsing a phase, a vertical scroll through all rows and a horizontal scroll. Post the numbers here. If it does not hold, file the engine ticket for the link layer with that reproducer and link it here as a blocker; the example then ships with the largest counts that do hold, or after the cut.
2. **A new folder `examples/gantt/bigData`:** a building project of 2,000 tasks in three levels (phases, work packages, tasks), with finish-to-start links inside a package and between packages, generated in the example from a fixed seed. The generator writes every parent's dates as the span of its children. The task count and the link count stand in the toolbar.
3. **It opens with the first phase expanded and the others collapsed,** so the first frame shows the tree, the bars and the links together.
4. **Editing stays on only if the profile shows that a task move with its cascade holds at this size.** Otherwise the example is read-only and says so; the pull request names which.
5. **One line says what to try,** for example "Expand a phase and scroll: the tree, the bars and the links keep up."
6. **A catalog record** `gantt-big-data` in the family `gantt`: a title that says what it shows ("A project of 2,000 tasks"), `feature` and `lookFor` in the form of its siblings, and a cover taken in the dark theme.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The profile's numbers are on this ticket before the pull request opens: first paint, expanding a phase, vertical and horizontal scroll, with the machine and the build mode.
- [ ] The example opens with 2,000 tasks, or the stated count that passed the profile, and their links; both counts are on screen; the data is seeded, so the first frame is the same on every load.
- [ ] Every parent's bar spans its children; a spec asserts it for one phase.
- [ ] A spec under `test/playwright/e2e/gantt/` asserts both counts, and that the rows in the DOM stay a small, stated fraction of the tasks.
- [ ] No console error. 1440 × 900 and 390 × 844. Every theme of the base example's `neo-config.json`.
- [ ] The pull request adds no data file.
- [ ] **Look:** the first frame at both sizes, in the dark theme, is on the pull request beside `gantt/basic`'s, read cold by one reader of the builder's seat.
- [ ] The cover is on `neomjs/pages` before the pull request merges, and the record publishes.

## Out of Scope

Engine changes: a defect the profile finds gets its own ticket, and so does deriving a parent's dates from its children. Working time, zoom levels and editing in the tree's cells: each is a candidate of its own in #21140. Loading from a server.

## Avoided Traps

- **Parent dates typed apart from their children.** The engine does not derive them, so a phase could end before its last task.
- **Counts the engine does not hold.** The numbers on screen are the ones that passed the profile.
- **A data file,** and **random data on each load:** the cover and the spec name first-frame content.

## Related

Parent #21346 · #21140 (the Gantt row of its content table) · #20874 and #20878 (the family) · `examples/grid/treeBigData`, the tree grid's scale example.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-11-18T22:44:28Z

**The profile, before the pull request** (Ada, the builder; AC 1)

The chart holds at 2,000 tasks and 1,972 links, so the example ships the full counts with editing on. No engine blocker. The one cost the profile found is filed as #21407, and its fix is PR #21408.

**Machine and build.** Apple M5 Max (18 cores, 128 GB), macOS 27.2.1, Node 25.9.0. Chromium 159.0.8154.6, headless, through Playwright 1.65.1 with the default launch flags. Viewport 1440 × 900, devmode (unbundled source, served by `buildScripts/util/fileServer.mjs`), 3 fresh browser contexts. Tree: `ada/21356-gantt-big-data` at `3a6a8a392f`, on `dev` `0b8d66fa17`.

**Method.** Every time is taken in the page. A measurement starts at the input event's own `timeStamp` (a real click or key press) and ends at `performance.now()` in the first animation frame whose DOM shows the result. That resolves to one frame (16.7 ms); a Playwright poll would round to its interval. "Settled" is the first frame after the chart's last DOM mutation.

**The data.** A building programme: 8 phases of 12 zones, four crews per zone working their bays in order. That is 1,896 tasks and 104 summaries, 2,000 rows in all, with 1,972 finish-to-start links. A fixed seed (Mulberry32) makes every load draw the same plan. It opens with phase 1 open: 257 visible rows.

| Metric | Run 1 | Run 2 | Run 3 | Median | DOM |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| First paint: navigation until bars, links and both counts are painted | 269.7 | 286.2 | 302.8 | **286.2 ms** | 25 + 25 rows, 25 bars, 215 links |
| Collapse phase 1 (249 rows): rows / links repainted | 40.2 / 56.9 | 44.1 / 60.9 | 44.8 / 61.5 | **44.1 / 60.9 ms** | |
| Expand phase 1: rows / links | 35.8 / 52.5 | 32.6 / 49.3 | 48.7 / 65.4 | **35.8 / 52.5 ms** | |
| Expand the last closed phase, reaching all 2,000 rows: rows / links | 44.0 / 60.7 | 39.9 / 56.5 | 42.0 / 58.6 | **42.0 / 58.6 ms** | 25 + 25 rows, 283 links |
| Vertical: 105 jumps of one viewport through all 2,000 rows, per jump p50 / p95 / max | 48.9 / 49.8 / 49.8 | 47.8 / 49.5 / 49.7 | 48.7 / 49.6 / 49.8 | **48.7 / 49.6 / 49.8 ms** | longest frame 16.8 ms |
| Vertical, continuous: one row per frame for 600 frames | 0 blank | 0 blank | 0 blank | **no blank frame** | longest frame 16.8 ms |
| Horizontal: 8 jumps of one viewport across the 9,979 px axis, all rows open, settled p50 / max | 47.5 / 61.1 | 47.5 / 48.0 | 48.3 / 49.2 | **47.5 / 49.2 ms** | links re-projected on 7 of 8 jumps, longest frame 16.8 ms |
| Move the first task one day by keyboard. Its cascade moves all 1,895 successors, then the example writes the 104 parent spans as one store batch. Settled | 514.0 | 513.9 | 513.5 | **513.9 ms** | the zone again spans its tasks |
| The same move with #21407's fix (PR #21408) | 96.3 | 96.8 | 98.6 | **96.8 ms** | |

**The link layer** is windowed horizontally only, as the source check on #21346 said. With all 2,000 rows open, the projected window (the 1,198 px viewport plus 400 px on each side) holds 132 to 536 links in its one SVG, which is 80,000 px tall. The horizontal sweep through those windows never took a frame longer than 16.8 ms.

**Editing.** Measured before the example wrote parents back, the cascade alone settled in 111.8, 79.8 and 96.9 ms (median 96.9). A parent keeps its stored dates (`Neo.gantt.Container`), so after an edit the example writes each touched zone and phase back to its children's span. Without #21408 every record of that batch re-projects all links, which makes the worst edit about half a second; with it, the same edit settles in 97 ms. Editing therefore stays on, and the pull request does not need #21408 to merge first.
